message.content:
Below are two ways you can provision a **Google Compute Engine** instance that has an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU and runs **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**.

> ⚠️ **Note**  
> * “EC2” is Amazon‑AWS terminology. In Google Cloud the equivalent service is **Compute Engine**.  
> * The RTX A6000 is only available in the **`nvidia-tesla-a100`** family of GPUs – Google does not offer an RTX A6000 SKU.  
>   The closest match is the **NVIDIA A100** (PCI‑e or SXM).  
> * You must have the **Compute Engine API** enabled, a billing account attached, and the `gcloud` CLI installed (or you can use the REST API directly).

---

## 1️⃣ Using the `gcloud` CLI

```bash
# 1. Set your project and zone
PROJECT_ID="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"

# 2. Create a VM with an A100 GPU (closest to RTX A6000)
gcloud compute instances create my-a100-instance \
    --project=${PROJECT_ID} \
    --zone=${ZONE} \
    --machine-type=n1-standard-8 \          # 8 vCPU, 30 GB RAM
    --accelerator=type=nvidia-tesla-a100,count=1 \
    --maintenance-policy=MIGRATE \
    --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \
    --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
    --boot-disk-size=200GB \
    --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd \
    --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform \
    --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh \
    --tags=http-server,https-server
```

### What each flag does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--machine-type` | CPU/RAM configuration (`n1-standard-8` gives 8 vCPUs & 30 GB RAM). |
| `--accelerator` | Adds a GPU. Replace `count=1` if you need more. |
| `--image-family` / `--image-project` | Installs Ubuntu 20.04 LTS from the official Ubuntu image repository. |
| `--boot-disk-size` / `--boot-disk-type` | SSD boot disk of 200 GB. |
| `--scopes` | Grants full Cloud Platform access (adjust scopes if you want tighter IAM). |
| `--metadata-from-file startup-script` | Optional: run a shell script at first boot. |

> 📌 **Tip** – If you need the **SXM** variant of the A100 (higher memory bandwidth), change the accelerator type to `nvidia-tesla-a100-sxm-80gb`.

---

## 2️⃣ Using the REST API (JSON)

If you prefer to call the API directly (e.g., from a CI/CD pipeline or a custom app), here’s a minimal JSON payload you can POST to:

```
POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/instances
Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN>
Content-Type: application/json
```

```json
{
  "name": "my-a100-instance",
  "machineType": "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 200,
        "diskType": "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a100"
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
    }
  ],
  "tags": {
    "items": ["http-server", "https-server"]
  },
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\napt-get update\napt-get install -y python3-pip"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

> 🔑 **Authentication** – Use OAuth 2.0 to obtain an access token (`gcloud auth print-access-token`) and pass it in the `Authorization` header.

---

## 3️⃣ Quick Checklist

| ✅ | Item |
|----|------|
| ✅ | Enable Compute Engine API (`gcloud services enable compute.googleapis.com`). |
| ✅ | Attach a billing account to your project. |
| ✅ | Ensure you have the necessary IAM permissions (`roles/compute.admin` or custom role). |
| ✅ | Verify the GPU quota for your region (`gcloud compute accelerator-types list --filter="region:{ZONE}"`). |
| ✅ | Optionally, pre‑install NVIDIA drivers via a startup script or use the **GPU‑optimized OS image** (`projects/nvidia-public/global/images/family/nvidia-ubuntu-2004-lts`). |

---

### Final Thoughts

* The **RTX A6000** isn’t offered by GCP; the **NVIDIA A100** is the closest high‑end GPU.  
* If you truly need an RTX A6000, consider **AWS** (where it’s available as `g5dn.xlarge` or similar).  
* Always monitor GPU usage and cost—GPUs can quickly drive up your bill.

Happy computing! 🚀
